vulnerability.title: Shutdown System When Auditing Failures Occur
vulnerability.description: If the auditd daemon is configured to use the augenrules program to read audit rules during daemon startup (the default), add the following line to to the bottom of a file with suffix .rules in the directory /etc/audit/rules.d: -f If the auditd daemon is configured to use the auditctl utility to read audit rules during daemon startup, add the following line to the bottom of the /etc/audit/audit.rules file: -f
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q audit && rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then var_audit_failure_mode='' # Traverse all of: # # /etc/audit/audit.rules, (for auditctl case) # /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules (for augenrules case) find /etc/audit /etc/audit/rules.d -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rules' -exec sed -i '/-f[[:space:]]\+.*/d' {} ';' for AUDIT_FILE in "/etc/audit/audit.rules" "/etc/audit/rules.d/immutable.rules" do echo '' >> $AUDIT_FILE echo '# Set the audit.rules configuration to halt system upon audit failure per security requirements' >> $AUDIT_FILE echo "-f $var_audit_failure_mode" >> $AUDIT_FILE done else >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done' fi
vulnerability.group: Configure auditd Rules for Comprehensive Auditing

triage_decision.reason: The remediation only adds or updates the '-f' audit failure mode line in audit rule files. This is a standard STIG audit rule change, does not affect authentication, networking, or critical services, and can be applied with a simple file edit and auditd restart.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: system will halt on audit failure (intended behavior)

reasoning_messages.reasoning:
We need to propose a plan to ensure audit failure mode -f is set. The description says add "-f" line to appropriate file(s). Need to check which mode audit daemon uses: augenrules or auditctl. Usually default is augenrules reading rules from /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules, which are compiled to /etc/audit/audit.rules. So we add "-f" to a .rules file, e.g., create a file /etc/audit/rules.d/audit_failure.rules with content "-f". Ensure not duplicate.

Plan: check if any .rules file already contains -f line. Use grep.

Steps:
1. read /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules to see if -f present. But we must read each file using read_file. Could read a generic file like /etc/audit/rules.d/sshd.rules? Might be many. Simpler: check if /etc/audit/rules.d/audit_failure.rules exists. If not, create it with "-f". If exists, ensure contains "-f". Possibly also modify /etc/audit/audit.rules if using auditctl.

But requirement: add to bottom of a file with suffix .rules in /etc/audit/rules.d. So create a new file.

Plan steps:
- read_file /etc/audit/rules.d/audit_failure.rules (if fails, it's not there).
- If content doesn't contain "-f", then write file with "-f\n".
- Then restart auditd: run_cmd "systemctl restart auditd".

Also ensure that we delete any existing -f lines in other files to avoid duplicates: use sed -i '/-f[[:space:]]*/d' on all .rules files. But careful to modify existing, but that's okay.

Thus plan includes:
1. For each file in /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules: run sed -i to delete any existing -f lines.
2. Ensure a dedicated file contains "-f".

But we can't loop directly; need to know file list. Could use find with -exec; but that's a command line with find; okay as single command. Example: run_cmd "find /etc/audit/rules.d -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.rules' -exec sed -i '/-f[[:space:]]\\+.*/d' {} \\;". That's one command with find and exec; allowed.

Then write file.

Now produce plan description.

Then call review_plan.

review_feedback: The plan removes existing "-f" lines and adds a new file with just "-f", but it does not specify the required failure mode value (e.g., "-f 1" for panic) and does not address the auditctl configuration (/etc/audit/audit.rules). Without a valid mode, auditd will not halt on failures, so the vulnerability remains.

Without a valid mode, auditd will not halt on failures, so the vulnerability remains.
concerns: Auditctl configuration file (/etc/audit/audit.rules) is not updated.
Potential for duplicate entries if other rule files contain "-f" lines that are not removed.
suggested_improvements: Write "-f 1" (or appropriate value) to the dedicated rule file.
Also update /etc/audit/audit.rules when auditd uses auditctl.
Ensure removal of "-f" lines from all rule files, including /etc/audit/audit.rules.
Add a step to verify the syntax with "auditctl -s" after restart.
